title: Baseline seed: permission catalog and global default reference template (idempotent, reset- and deploy-safe)
objective: Port the .NET startup seeding to an idempotent baseline seed applied on every local reset and runnable as a deploy step: the fixed permission catalog and the Internal-managed global default reference template (M-11 layer 1).
scope: Baseline seed content: full permission catalog (identical keys/names to the .NET seed) and default_reference_items global template rows (all list types with their guarded status defaults, reporting categories, canonical keys, terminal flags, sort orders)
Delivery mechanism: supabase/seed.sql wired into supabase db reset AND an idempotent scripts/db/seed.ts baseline mode runnable against any environment via DIRECT_DATABASE_URL (Q-8)
Idempotency: re-running converges (upsert on stable natural keys); never duplicates rows
npm scripts: db:seed (baseline), documented in docs/local-development.md
out_of_scope: Tenant-creation-time copying of the template into a tenant (T-016)
implementation_details: Extract the authoritative permission catalog and default reference template from the .NET seeding code (behavioral reference) — every permission key used by RequirePermission policies and UI gating must exist.

seed.sql uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (natural key) DO UPDATE for catalog rows so resets and re-runs converge; scripts/db/seed.ts (tsx) shares the same SQL or generates it, taking --baseline flag; connects via DIRECT_DATABASE_URL (never the pooler for admin work, A-8).
Do not auto-run against production: script requires explicit --env confirmation for non-local targets (M-11 'never run automatically in production').
Record seed version/hash in a small seed_meta row if useful for verifying convergence in tests (optional, keep simple).
Guarded defaults must satisfy P-04: canonical keys and reporting categories for lead/quote statuses exactly match the reference implementation (dashboards and the legality matrix depend on them).

unit: None (data + script; convergence covered at integration level)
integration: supabase db reset yields the full permission catalog and global template; row counts and canonical keys match the reference inventory
Running db:seed twice produces identical state (row-level diff empty) — idempotency (N-06)
seed.ts runs against a second scratch database via DIRECT_DATABASE_URL proving the deployed-environment path (Q-8)
e2e: None directly; downstream suites depend on this seed

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to M-11 (baseline layer), Q-8, P-03 (catalog), P-04 (template).
Delegated to Implementor. T-006 and T-008 run in parallel (seed content vs src/server/lib/db). Orchestrator owns harness JSON.

Baseline seed implemented: 81-code permission catalog + 93-row/10-list global default template, SQL mechanically GENERATED from PermissionCatalog.cs and DefaultReferenceData.cs rather than transcribed, so no key was retyped. Orchestrator independently confirmed 81 permissions / 93 template rows / 10 lists in the DB against 81 unique codes in PermissionCatalog.cs. Verification does not trust the extraction: tests/helpers/dotnet-seed-reference.ts RE-PARSES the C# independently and asserts the whole set (so a swapped pair still fails), with a guard test requiring >50 parsed codes so an empty expected set cannot vacuously pass. Cross-checked against every PermissionCatalog.X.Y and RequirePermission literal in src/api: 79 referenced, 0 referenced-but-missing; the 2 catalog-only codes (brokers.manage_api_access, leads.delete) are documented as reserved in the C# source. DESIGN DECISION worth review: conflict behaviour deliberately differs per table to match the two .NET seeders - permissions uses ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (code-owned catalog), default_reference_items uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING because DefaultTemplateSeeder must never overwrite Internal users' template edits (P-04); DO UPDATE there would silently revert edits on every deploy. Single source of truth: seed.ts extracts the marked block from seed.sql rather than carrying a second copy, so reset and deploy paths cannot drift. 5 mutants all RED - mutant 3 (remove ON CONFLICT) initially SURVIVED because the static conflict-tolerance scan matched the file header's prose explanation instead of the statement; fixed by stripping SQL comments first. Implementor also closed a second blind spot pre-emptively: seeds never delete, so a row dropped from seed.sql would linger in an already-seeded DB and keep DB-level assertions green until the next reset - static file-vs-.NET parity checks now catch that without a reset. Idempotency proven: re-run yields identical counts (81/93). Production safety: non-local APP_ENV refuses without a matching --env, and a MISMATCHED flag also refuses (a stale --env=local cannot seed production); test drives the real CLI and asserts the DB digest is unchanged after refusal. db:validate needed no snapshot refresh (seeding writes data, not schema).

Evaluator PASS at iteration 0, no findings. RULING (asymmetric conflict behaviour): CONFIRMED as the faithful port, not an inconsistency. Read both .NET seeders directly: PermissionCatalogSeeder.cs updates Category/Description of existing rows every startup ('the catalog in code is the source of truth') and never deletes -> ON CONFLICT (code) DO UPDATE is exact; DefaultTemplateSeeder.cs inserts only rows missing by (list_type,name) and 'never overwrites a value an Internal user has since edited' (P-04) -> ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is exact. DO UPDATE on default_reference_items would silently revert Internal template edits on every deploy - the asymmetry is required. Independent verification: supabase:reset exit 0; db:seed run twice, digests (identity ids included) byte-identical across runs (permissions md5 950601ab..., items md5 3577c1e9...), 81/93 rows both times; db:validate exit 0 (double-reset schema convergence); full suite 38 files/594 tests 0 skipped exit 0; typecheck 0; lint 0; stub cron:list exits 1. MUTANTS REPRODUCED FIRST-HAND: (1) stripped ON CONFLICT from the permissions INSERT while the header PROSE still said 'ON CONFLICT' - the repaired comment-stripping scan went red (killed; the pre-fix false-green shape is genuinely closed); (2) deleted the quotes.withdraw row from seed.sql WITHOUT a reset - the static file-vs-.NET parity check went red (expected 80 to be 81), proving the delete blind spot is closed without needing a reset. Both mutants restored byte-identical (cmp verified). C# re-parse verified: whole-set equality (sorted arrays, not counts), >50-codes guard plus a constants-vs-All count cross-check make a vacuous pass impossible; commented-out seed rows cannot satisfy the parity regex (anchored at line start). Production safety re-run in isolation: APP_ENV=production without --env refuses (exit!=0, names --env=production), APP_ENV=staging with mismatched --env=local refuses, and the DB digest is asserted unchanged after refusal - all via the real CLI. Catalog-only codes: brokers.manage_api_access carries an explicit 'Reserved for T-030' doc comment; leads.delete has no 'reserved' comment but is an ordinary unreferenced catalog constant - the history note's 'documented as reserved' is half-accurate but immaterial (whole-set parity governs). Security: no findings - connection strings never logged, refusal path exits non-zero, seed runs in one transaction over DIRECT_DATABASE_URL, no secrets in seed content. AC-009/AC-086 (T-006 share) and V-010/V-110 (T-006 share) satisfied; demo-seed halves remain with T-041.
